title: Command views render a blank/black main panel with no form on first navigation
detail: The dominant UX defect class: several views (t2i, video-quality, video-generate, faceswap, model-check, jobs) render an empty black void on first load because CommandForm only mounts AFTER useDefaultState resolves server defaults, and the canvas is bare in the meantime. There is no header, breadcrumb, empty-state, or loading skeleton — the user cannot tell a loading failure from an empty state from a broken render. Affects every createCommandView() view until guarded. The VLM caption reads these as 'a large, empty black panel' / 'no primary action button visible'.

title: Guard CommandViewShell with an actionable empty-state instead of a dead black panel
detail: Adopted fix for blank-panel views: when a view yields no form children (silent render failure), CommandViewShell now renders an actionable 'This view has nothing to show' message plus a .empty-view-state CSS class, so the canvas is never a bare void. Applied to video-quality-01 (score held 2->2 but the panel is no longer dead). Generalizes to every createCommandView view — always provide a non-blocking empty/loading placeholder while useDefaultState resolves or when children fail to mount.

title: Wrap command views in a persistent title header (reuse ModelCheckView inline-style convention)
detail: Adopted fix for blank/unlabeled panels: wrap the generated view (e.g. T2lView) in a container that renders a persistent h2 title plus a dim description line, matching the existing ModelCheckView inline-style convention and reusing --text-bright/--text-dim CSS variables. Result: the main panel is never blank/unlabeled and the user can always tell which view is active. Applied to t2i-01 (score 3->9). This is the higher-impact sibling of the empty-state guard — it also labels healthy renders.

title: Sidebar active-state logic is correct; the CSS is too faint for the VLM (and users) to read as selected
detail: Layout.tsx already computes an `active` class on the sidebar item when currentView.action===cmd.id, so the routing logic is NOT the bug. The defect is that .sidebar-item.active (global.css:91) uses only a faint background + accent left border + accent text that reads as indistinguishable from inactive. Strengthen with an --accent color-mix tinted background + font-weight 600 (adopted in video-quality-02, score 2->8) so the selected item is unmistakable. Do NOT re-investigate the Layout logic when the active cue looks missing.

title: toSections silently discards any schema field without a `section` property
detail: Latent trap: schemas/toForm.ts toSections does `if (!f.section) continue;`, so any field lacking a `section` is silently dropped from the rendered form with NO error. Confirmed instance: faceswap schema's 'LoRA Path' field {key:'lora'} has no section, so the documented LoRA control never appears in the UI and users cannot set a custom face-swap LoRA despite the schema declaring it. Either assign every schema field a section, or make toSections fall back to a default 'Advanced' section instead of dropping sectionless fields.

title: ViewDescriptor id MUST equal the useCommandJob/SCHEMA_MAP action key
detail: Latent routing/state bug: VideoGenerateView registers with descriptor id 'vid-generate', but every other reference uses 'video-generate' (useCommandJob('video-generate'), action='video-generate', SCHEMA_MAP['video-generate']). If routing or useDefaultState keys off the descriptor id, the schema-defaults fetch and action routing resolve against different keys — contributing to blank render and breaking per-view state persistence. Convention: keep the descriptor id identical to the schema action key AND the CLI action, as the sibling video views (VideoRelay etc.) already do.

title: Disabled submit buttons give no reason — no inline hint listing missing required inputs
detail: Recurring UX gap: schema.isDisabled(state) returns true when required inputs are unset (e.g. faceswap input_image/face), greying out the primary action, but nothing in the UI explains WHY or what the user must do. No required-field callout, no helper text, no 'Upload X and Y to enable Z'. A first-time user staring at a disabled button has no path forward. When schema.isDisabled(state) is true, render an InlineError or small hint near the btn-row listing the missing required inputs.

title: Sidebar nav items are non-semantic divs — not keyboard-focusable, no aria-current
detail: Accessibility defect: all navigation entries (Gallery, Config, Jobs, every command) are plain <div> elements with onClick handlers (Layout.tsx). No role='button', no tabIndex, no aria-current — invisible to Tab-key navigation and screen readers cannot announce them. The sidebar <aside> is also not a <nav aria-label>. Fix: render nav items as <button> (or role='button' tabIndex={0} + onKeyDown Enter/Space), wrap in <nav aria-label='Views'>, set aria-current='page' on the active item. A keyboard-only or assistive-tech user cannot reach any view currently.

title: Avg UX score 4.82 -> 5.36 in 3 iters; ~17 high-severity issues remain — needs ~8 iters to reach ~7.0
detail: Measured baseline from the 23-view scan: avg UX score 4.82, 151 issues total (20 high). With maxIters:3 and dryRun:false, only 3 fixes applied (score ceiling 5.36), leaving 17 high-severity issues unfixed. The blank-panel/active-nav/header fixes each move a single view 3-7 points, so the lever-per-iter ratio is high but the volume of low-scoring views (t2i=3, video-quality=2, video-generate=3, faceswap=3, image-restore=4, model-check=4) exceeds a 3-iter budget. Suggested next run: maxIters:8, dryRun:false -> expect avg ~7.0. image-pipeline scored null/0 issues (healthy / not reached) and can be skipped to save budget.

title: VLM caption can misread a correctly-wired feature as missing when the visual cue is too subtle
detail: Recurring false-positive class: the VLM (and by extension users) reports 'No active/selected highlight' and 'no primary action button visible' even when the underlying TS logic is correct. video-quality-02 and t2i-02 both reported a missing active-nav cue, but Layout.tsx already applies the `active` class — the CSS was just too faint. Treat 'feature is missing' captions as visual-prominence problems first (strengthen the CSS) before investigating the logic. Distinguish 'logic absent' from 'logic present but invisible' by reading the source, not by trusting the caption.
